import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zilber–Pink conjecture

The Zilber–Pink conjecture states that if $X$ is a mixed Shimura variety or a semiabelian
variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$, and $V \subseteq X$ is a subvariety, then $V$ contains only
finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.

Here a *special subvariety* of a semiabelian variety $X$ is a translate of an irreducible
algebraic subgroup of $X$ by a torsion point, and an *atypical subvariety* of $V$ is an
irreducible component $Z$ of an intersection $V \cap T$ with $T \subseteq X$ special such that
$\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$.

This file states the semiabelian case (due independently to Zilber and to
Bombieri–Masser–Zannier for tori, and to Pink in general). It implies the Manin–Mumford and
Mordell–Lang conjectures. The mixed Shimura case (Pink's conjecture) is not stated: mixed Shimura
varieties are not available in Mathlib.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Zilber–Pink conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zilber%E2%80%93Pink_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Zi02] B. Zilber, *Exponential sums equations and the Schanuel conjecture*,
  J. London Math. Soc. 65 (2002), 27–44.
- [BMZ07] E. Bombieri, D. Masser, U. Zannier, *Anomalous subvarieties—structure theorems and
  applications*, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2007.
- [Pi05] R. Pink, *A combination of the conjectures of Mordell–Lang and André–Oort*, in
  *Geometric Methods in Algebra and Number Theory*, Progr. Math. 235 (2005), 251–282.
- [HP16] P. Habegger, J. Pila, *O-minimality and certain atypical intersections*,
  Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 49 (2016), 813–858.
-/

namespace ZilberPinkConjecture

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Limits
open scoped MonObj

noncomputable section

/-- The base scheme $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$. -/
local notation "𝕊" => Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)

/- Throughout, `G` is a group scheme over `ℂ`: a scheme `G` over `𝕊 = Spec ℂ` together with a
group object structure on `G` in the category of `𝕊`-schemes. Its `ℂ`-points are the
`𝕊`-morphisms `𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊`, i.e. the sections `Spec ℂ ⟶ G` of the structure
morphism; they form a group. -/
variable (G : Scheme.{0}) [G.Over 𝕊] [GrpObj (G.asOver 𝕊)]

/-- Left translation of `G` by the `ℂ`-point `x`, as a morphism of `ℂ`-schemes `G ⟶ G`.
On `ℂ`-points it is `g ↦ x * g`. -/
def translation (x : 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊) : G.asOver 𝕊 ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊 :=
  lift (toUnit _ ≫ x) (𝟙 _) ≫ μ

/-- Translation by the identity is the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem translation_one : translation G 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
  change (toUnit _ ≫ (1 : 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊)) * 𝟙 _ = 𝟙 _
  rw [Hom.one_def, ← Category.assoc, toUnit_unique (toUnit _ ≫ toUnit _) (toUnit _), ← Hom.one_def,
    one_mul]

/-- Translation by a product is the composite of the translations. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 14]
theorem translation_mul (x y : 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊) :
    translation G (x * y) = translation G y ≫ translation G x := by
  change (toUnit _ ≫ (x * y)) * 𝟙 _ = translation G y ≫ ((toUnit _ ≫ x) * 𝟙 _)
  rw [MonObj.comp_mul (translation G y), Category.comp_id, ← Category.assoc,
    toUnit_unique (translation G y ≫ toUnit _) (toUnit _), MonObj.comp_mul, mul_assoc]
  rfl

/-- A subset `H` of the underlying space of `G` is an *algebraic subgroup* of `G` if it is
Zariski closed and the `ℂ`-points of `G` lying in `H` form a subgroup of the group of
`ℂ`-points of `G`. Since `ℂ` is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, these are exactly
the underlying sets of the closed subgroup schemes of `G`. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Set G) : Prop :=
  IsClosed H ∧ ∃ H' : Subgroup (𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊), ∀ x, x ∈ H' ↔ Set.range x.left.base ⊆ H

/-- `G` is an algebraic subgroup of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 11 14]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ : IsAlgebraicSubgroup G Set.univ :=
  ⟨isClosed_univ, ⊤, by simp⟩

/-- A subset `T` of the underlying space of `G` is a *special subvariety* if it is the translate
of an irreducible algebraic subgroup of `G` by a torsion `ℂ`-point of `G`. -/
def IsSpecialSubvariety (T : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ (x : 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ G.asOver 𝕊) (H : Set G), IsOfFinOrder x ∧ IsAlgebraicSubgroup G H ∧
    IsIrreducible H ∧ T = (translation G x).left.base '' H

/-- An integral group scheme `G` over `ℂ` is a special subvariety of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 11 14]
theorem isSpecialSubvariety_univ [IsIntegral G] : IsSpecialSubvariety G Set.univ :=
  ⟨1, Set.univ, IsOfFinOrder.one, isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ G,
    IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ G, by simp [translation_one]⟩

/-- `Z` is an *atypical subvariety* of `V ⊆ G` if it is an irreducible component of an
intersection `V ∩ T`, where `T ⊆ G` is a special subvariety, and
$\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim G$, dimensions being Krull dimensions of the Zariski topology.
The inequality is written as $\dim V + \dim T < \dim Z + \dim G$ to avoid subtraction in
`WithBot ℕ∞`. -/
def IsAtypicalSubvariety (V Z : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set G, IsSpecialSubvariety G T ∧ Maximal (fun W ↦ IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ V ∩ T) Z ∧
    topologicalKrullDim V + topologicalKrullDim T < topologicalKrullDim Z + topologicalKrullDim G

/-- `G` is a *semiabelian variety* over `ℂ`.

A semiabelian variety is a connected commutative algebraic group `G` which is an extension of
an abelian variety by an algebraic torus. Since neither tori nor abelian varieties are available
in Mathlib, we use the following equivalent characterisation: a commutative group variety
(integral, separated, of finite type) over `ℂ` is semiabelian if and only if every
`ℂ`-morphism from the affine line `𝔸¹` to `G` is constant.

Indeed, by Chevalley's structure theorem the maximal connected affine subgroup `L` of `G` has
`G / L` an abelian variety, and, `ℂ` having characteristic zero, `L ≅ T × 𝔾ₐⁿ` with `T` a torus.
If `n = 0` then `G` is semiabelian; if `n > 0` then `𝔾ₐ ↪ G` is a non-constant morphism from
`𝔸¹`. Conversely if `G` is an extension of an abelian variety `A` by a torus `T`, a morphism
`𝔸¹ → G` composed with `G → A` is constant (abelian varieties contain no rational curves), so it
lands in a fibre, which is isomorphic to `T ≅ 𝔾ₘᵗ`, and every morphism `𝔸¹ → 𝔾ₘᵗ` is constant
since the units of `ℂ[x]` are the constants. -/
structure IsSemiabelianVariety : Prop where
  /-- The group law is commutative. -/
  isCommMonObj : IsCommMonObj (G.asOver 𝕊)
  /-- `G` is integral, i.e. irreducible and reduced (for a group scheme of finite type over `ℂ`
  this is equivalent to `G` being connected). -/
  isIntegral : IsIntegral G
  /-- `G` is locally of finite type over `ℂ`. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (G ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- `G` is quasi-compact. -/
  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact (G ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- `G` is separated over `ℂ`. -/
  isSeparated : IsSeparated (G ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- Every `ℂ`-morphism from the affine line to `G` is constant. -/
  base_const_of_isOver (f : 𝔸(Fin 1; 𝕊) ⟶ G) (hf : f.IsOver 𝕊) (a b : 𝔸(Fin 1; 𝕊)) :
    f.base a = f.base b

/-- **Zilber–Pink conjecture** (semiabelian case, Zilber / Bombieri–Masser–Zannier / Pink).
Let $X$ be a semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $V \subseteq X$ be a
subvariety (a Zariski closed irreducible subset). Then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal
atypical subvarieties, where an atypical subvariety of $V$ is an irreducible component $Z$ of an
intersection $V \cap T$, with $T \subseteq X$ a special subvariety (a translate of an irreducible
algebraic subgroup of $X$ by a torsion point), such that
$\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.ii (hG : IsSemiabelianVariety G) (V : Set G)
    (hV : IsClosed V) (hV' : IsIrreducible V) :
    {Z : Set G | Maximal (IsAtypicalSubvariety G V) Z}.Finite := by
  sorry

end

end ZilberPinkConjecture

subgroups by torsion points.

The mixed Shimura case (Pink's conjecture) is not stated: mixed Shimura varieties and their
special subvarieties are not available in Mathlib.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Zilber–Pink conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zilber%E2%80%93Pink_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- B. Zilber, *Exponential sums equations and the Schanuel conjecture*, J. London Math. Soc. (2)
  65 (2002), 27–44.
- E. Bombieri, D. Masser, U. Zannier, *Anomalous subvarieties—structure theorems and
  applications*, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2007, no. 19.
- R. Pink, *A common generalization of the conjectures of André-Oort, Manin-Mumford, and
  Mordell-Lang*, preprint (2005).
-/

namespace ZilberPinkConjecture

open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory AlgebraicGeometry
open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj

/-- The base scheme $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$. -/
local notation "𝕊" => Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)

/- We work with a scheme `X` over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$ that is a group scheme over
$\mathbb{C}$, i.e. a group object in the category of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$.
The Zariski topology on `X` is the topology of its underlying space, and the dimension of a
subset is its topological Krull dimension. -/

variable (X : Scheme) [X.Over 𝕊] [GrpObj (X.asOver 𝕊)]

/-- The $\mathbb{C}$-points of `X`: the morphisms from the terminal object of the category
of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$ to `X`, i.e. the sections of the structure
morphism. Since `X` is a group scheme, this is a group (the group $X(\mathbb{C})$). -/
abbrev Points := 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊

/-- The point of the underlying space of `X` corresponding to a $\mathbb{C}$-point. -/
def Points.toPoint (x : Points X) : X := x.left.base (default : 𝕊)

/-- An *algebraic subgroup* of `X`: a Zariski-closed subset `H` of `X` whose
$\mathbb{C}$-points form a subgroup of $X(\mathbb{C})$. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Set X) : Prop :=
  IsClosed H ∧ ∃ K : Subgroup (Points X), ∀ x : Points X, x ∈ K ↔ x.toPoint ∈ H

/-- `X` is a *semiabelian variety* over $\mathbb{C}$: a connected commutative algebraic group
over $\mathbb{C}$ (a commutative group scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$
with irreducible underlying space) that is an extension of an abelian variety by an algebraic
torus.

By Chevalley's structure theorem, a connected commutative algebraic group $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$
has a largest connected affine algebraic subgroup $L \cong \mathbb{G}_m^r \times \mathbb{G}_a^s$,
with $X / L$ an abelian variety; $X$ is semiabelian if and only if $s = 0$, i.e. if and only if
$X$ contains no algebraic subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$. Since $\mathbb{G}_a(\mathbb{C})$
is torsion-free, while every nontrivial connected algebraic subgroup of a semiabelian variety is
semiabelian and hence has nontrivial torsion, this is equivalent to the condition used here:
every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of $X$ contains a nontrivial torsion point. -/
structure IsSemiabelianVariety : Prop where
  /-- `X` is locally of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- `X` is quasi-compact; together with the previous field, `X` is of finite type over
  $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  compactSpace : CompactSpace X
  /-- `X` is connected (equivalently, irreducible). -/
  irreducibleSpace : IrreducibleSpace X
  /-- The group law of `X` is commutative. -/
  isCommMonObj : IsCommMonObj (X.asOver 𝕊)
  /-- Every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of `X` contains a nontrivial torsion
  point. -/
  exists_isOfFinOrder : ∀ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H → IsIrreducible H →
    (∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H) →
    ∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ IsOfFinOrder x ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H

/-- Translation $y \mapsto a \cdot y$ by the $\mathbb{C}$-point `a`, as an automorphism of the
$\mathbb{C}$-scheme `X`. -/
noncomputable def translation (a : Points X) : X.asOver 𝕊 ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊 :=
  lift (toUnit _ ≫ a) (𝟙 _) ≫ μ

/-- A *special subvariety* of the semiabelian variety `X`: the translate $a \cdot H$ of an
irreducible algebraic subgroup `H` of `X` by a torsion point `a`. -/
def IsSpecialSubvariety (T : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H ∧ IsIrreducible H ∧
    ∃ a : Points X, IsOfFinOrder a ∧ T = (translation X a).left.base '' H

/-- `Z` is an *atypical subvariety* of `V`: an irreducible component of $V \cap T$ for some
special subvariety `T` of `X`, with $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$, i.e.
$\dim V + \dim T < \dim Z + \dim X$. -/
def IsAtypicalSubvariety (V Z : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set X, IsSpecialSubvariety X T ∧ Maximal (fun W => IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ V ∩ T) Z ∧
    topologicalKrullDim V + topologicalKrullDim T < topologicalKrullDim Z + topologicalKrullDim X

/-- Composing a $\mathbb{C}$-point `y` with the translation by `a` gives the product `a * y`
in the group $X(\mathbb{C})$. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem comp_translation (a y : Points X) : (y ≫ translation X a : Points X) = a * y := by
  simp only [translation, Hom.mul_def, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
  congr 2
  simp

/-- The whole of `X` is an algebraic subgroup of `X`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ : IsAlgebraicSubgroup X Set.univ :=
  ⟨isClosed_univ, ⊤, by simp⟩

/-- **Zilber–Pink conjecture**, semiabelian case (Zilber; Bombieri–Masser–Zannier).

Let $X$ be a semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $V \subseteq X$ be a
subvariety (an irreducible Zariski-closed subset). Then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal
atypical subvarieties. Here an atypical subvariety of $V$ is an irreducible component $Z$ of
$V \cap T$, where $T \subseteq X$ is a special subvariety (a translate of an irreducible algebraic
subgroup of $X$ by a torsion point), such that $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$; maximality
is with respect to inclusion among the atypical subvarieties of $V$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.ii (hX : IsSemiabelianVariety X) (V : Set X)
    (hV : IsClosed V) (hV' : IsIrreducible V) :
    {Z : Set X | Maximal (IsAtypicalSubvariety X V) Z}.Finite := by
  sorry

end ZilberPinkConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None of substance. Note that slot (i)'s text_span is the entire list-page sentence (including the semiabelian clause) while its notes restrict it to the mixed-Shimura case; I followed the notes, treating (i) as the mixed-Shimura case (omitted: missing primitives) and (ii) as the semiabelian case.
modeling_decisions: Semiabelian variety is defined by a characterization rather than as an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (neither exists in Mathlib): a connected commutative group scheme of finite type over ℂ in which every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup has a nontrivial torsion point. Justification (Chevalley): the maximal connected affine subgroup is 𝔾_m^r × 𝔾_a^s and X is semiabelian iff s = 0; 𝔾_a(ℂ) is torsion-free, while nontrivial connected algebraic subgroups of semiabelian varieties are semiabelian and have torsion. A reviewer should check this equivalence.

Algebraic groups over ℂ are modeled as group objects `GrpObj (X.asOver (Spec ℂ))` in `Over (Spec ℂ)`; finite type is expressed as `LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec ℂ)` plus `CompactSpace X`; connectedness as `IrreducibleSpace X` (equivalent for group schemes over a field). Separatedness/reducedness are omitted as automatic over ℂ.

Algebraic subgroups are Zariski-closed subsets whose ℂ-points form a subgroup of X(ℂ) (set-level, not scheme-theoretic); over ℂ this coincides with underlying sets of (reduced) closed subgroup schemes, which is what the conjecture concerns.

Special subvarieties are torsion translates a·H of irreducible algebraic subgroups, following the Wikipedia article (rather than Pink's variant with all algebraic subgroups/cosets, which the notes say is equivalent for the finiteness claim). The translate is the image of H under the translation automorphism of X.
'Subvariety' V is taken to be an irreducible Zariski-closed subset of X (standard usage in Pink/Zilber/Bombieri–Masser–Zannier); the version for reducible closed V follows from the irreducible one.

Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions (in `WithBot ℕ∞`) of subsets of the underlying space; the atypicality inequality dim Z > dim V + dim T − dim X is written additively as dim V + dim T < dim Z + dim X, which is equivalent since all four dimensions are finite and non-⊥ (V, T, Z nonempty, X finite type over ℂ).
Irreducible components of V ∩ T are expressed as ⊆-maximal irreducible subsets of V ∩ T; 'maximal atypical subvarieties' are ⊆-maximal elements of the set of atypical subvarieties of V.

Only Points X (the ℂ-points as sections of the structure morphism) are used to define torsion and subgroup properties; closed points of a finite-type ℂ-scheme are exactly images of ℂ-points, so no information is lost.

attempts.decomposition_objections: Minor: the text_span of slot (i) is the entire list entry (it literally includes the semiabelian case), while its notes restrict it to the mixed-Shimura case; slot (ii)'s span is the semiabelian tail. The intended split (Pink's Shimura-variety conjecture vs. the semiabelian/CIT conjecture) is clear from the notes and I conformed to it. No substantive objection: the two cases genuinely need different primitives (Shimura varieties vs. semiabelian varieties), and the note that the semiabelian case is not a special case of the Shimura case matches the article.
modeling_decisions: No candidate file was written: every slot bails out with missing_primitives, as instructed.

Considered and rejected modelling a group scheme over C as `Grp_ (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)))` (the cartesian monoidal structure on `Over S` exists in Mathlib). It was rejected because the definition of a semiabelian variety additionally needs algebraic tori (G_m^n as a group object, which has no Mathlib construction), abelian varieties, and kernels/quotients of group schemes, none of which exist; a substitute definition via a structure theorem (e.g. 'connected commutative algebraic group with Zariski-dense torsion') would rest on a deep theorem and not be a faithful rendering of the stated conjecture.

Considered and rejected stating only the algebraic-torus case (Zilber's CIT over (C^*)^n), which could plausibly be built from MvPolynomial/Zariski topology; it is a strict special case and not one of the slots, so stating it under a slot name would be a misformalization.

Dimension and irreducible components could in principle be modelled with `topologicalKrullDim` and `irreducibleComponents` (both in Mathlib), but these are useless without the ambient special varieties.

zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.i.why: The statement requires (mixed) Shimura varieties over C together with their special subvarieties. Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has Shimura data, Hermitian symmetric domains, Shimura varieties (pure or mixed), their algebraic (Baily–Borel) structure, or special subvarieties. Searches (rg -i 'Shimura|Hermitian symmetric|symmetric domain|arithmetic subgroup') only hit congruence/arithmetic subgroups of SL_2(Z) acting on the upper half-plane (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/*), which is nowhere near sufficient to define a general mixed Shimura variety, its dimension, or its special subvarieties. Building this theory bespoke in a problem file is infeasible and could not be done faithfully, so the slot is omitted.

zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.ii.why: The statement requires semiabelian varieties over C (extensions of an abelian variety by an algebraic torus), their irreducible algebraic subgroups, torsion translates, closed subvarieties with dimensions and irreducible components. Mathlib has no algebraic groups/group schemes as a developed notion, no abelian varieties, no algebraic tori (not even G_m as a group scheme: there is no Hopf-algebra -> group-scheme functor, so G_m^n as a `Grp_ (Over (Spec C))` would have to be constructed with full proofs of the group-object axioms), and no kernels/quotients of group schemes. The only raw block available is `CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over S)` for schemes (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Pullbacks.lean), giving the bare type `Grp_ (Over (Spec C))`; defining 'semiabelian' on top of it would require either the missing torus/abelian-variety primitives or a replacement by a nontrivial theorem-based characterization (e.g. Zariski density of torsion points), which would not be a faithful rendering of the source definition. FormalConjecturesForMathlib also contains nothing relevant (rg -i 'semiabelian|abelian variet|algebraic group|Grp_|torus' finds nothing). Restricting to the algebraic-torus (CIT) case over (C^*)^n would state a strictly weaker theorem than the slot, so the slot is omitted rather than misstated.

modeling_decisions: The intended precise reading was the one supplied by the article and decomposition notes: an atypical subvariety is an irreducible component Z of V ∩ T for a special T, satisfying dim Z > dim V + dim T − dim X, and maximality is under inclusion among atypical subvarieties of V.
For the mixed-Shimura slot, “special” must retain its arithmetic Shimura-theoretic meaning; it cannot be modeled as an arbitrary predicate on closed subsets.

For the semiabelian slot, “special” was read as a torsion translate of an irreducible algebraic subgroup, as specified in the decomposition notes. This case was kept separate from the mixed-Shimura case because the source explicitly says it is not generally a special case.

zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.i.why: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib do not define mixed Shimura data/varieties or their special subvarieties. Although generic schemes, irreducible closed subsets, Krull dimension, and maximality are available, they are insufficient to characterize the ambient varieties and the arithmetically defined family of special subvarieties. Introducing a structure that merely labels an arbitrary scheme and arbitrary subsets as mixed Shimura/special would overgeneralize the conjecture and is not a faithful definition.

zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.ii.why: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib do not define algebraic group schemes, algebraic tori, abelian varieties/schemes, semiabelian varieties as extensions, algebraic subgroups, torsion translates, or the corresponding special subvarieties. Generic internal commutative group objects exist, but the geometric properties and exact-extension machinery needed to characterize semiabelian varieties are absent. An unconstrained wrapper around a scheme and a chosen family of subsets would not faithfully express the conjecture.
